$comment: Glossary terms: the single source for /glossary, the term pages' generated blocks, hub key terms and rule-page backlinks. Edit here, then run `bun scripts/glossary.ts --write`. format=page gets /glossary/<slug> once that page is written; format=entry is an A to Z entry on /glossary only. rules are docs rule ids (the **Rule ID** row of a rule page). Seeded from the 119-term plan, rule ids verified against the docs rule pages.

terms.title: What is robots.txt? Rules, syntax and common mistakes
terms.definition: A plain-text file at the site root that tells crawlers which paths they may fetch, per user-agent token (RFC 9309).
terms.grounding_note: robots.txt controls crawling, not indexing; a blocked URL can still be indexed from links.

terms.title: What is an XML sitemap? Format, limits and checks
terms.definition: An XML file listing the URLs a site wants crawled, with optional lastmod dates, referenced from robots.txt or submitted to search engines.

terms.title: Sitemap lastmod: what it means and when it is ignored
terms.definition: The optional `<lastmod>` date on a sitemap URL entry, meant to say when the page content last changed.

terms.title: What does noindex do? Meta tag, header and conflicts
terms.definition: A robots directive, in a meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header, that asks search engines to keep a page out of their index.

terms.title: Robots meta tag: directives, defaults and conflicts
terms.definition: A `<meta name="robots">` tag carrying page-level directives such as noindex, nofollow, nosnippet and max-snippet.
An HTTP response header that carries the same directives as the robots meta tag, and works for non-HTML files such as PDFs.

terms.title: What is indexability? Why a page is not indexed
terms.definition: Whether a crawled URL is eligible to be indexed: reachable, a 200 response, not noindexed, not blocked and not canonicalised elsewhere.

terms.title: What is crawl budget? When it matters and what wastes it
terms.definition: The number of URLs a search engine is willing and able to crawl on a site in a given time, set by crawl capacity and crawl demand.
terms.grounding_note: Google says crawl budget is a concern mainly for very large or fast-changing sites; say so.

terms.definition: A page that tells the visitor it does not exist (or is empty) while the server answers HTTP 200.

terms.title: Redirect chains: what they cost and how to flatten them
terms.definition: A sequence of two or more redirects between the requested URL and the final response.

terms.title: HTTP status codes for site audits: 3xx, 4xx and 5xx
terms.definition: The three-digit code a server returns with every response; 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.
Splitting a long list across numbered URLs; each page should be crawlable and canonicalise to itself.
The byte limit after which Googlebot stops reading a fetched HTML file or PDF; content past it is not indexed.
terms.grounding_note: Quote the limits exactly as the rule pages state them; the limits changed in 2026.

terms.title: What is a canonical URL? rel=canonical explained
terms.definition: The URL a page declares, with `<link rel="canonical">` or a Link header, as the preferred address for its content.

terms.title: Duplicate content: causes, myths and how to consolidate
terms.definition: The same or near-identical content reachable at more than one URL, or repeated titles and descriptions across pages.

terms.title: Title tag: length, uniqueness and what search shows
terms.definition: The `<title>` element in the page head; browsers show it in the tab and search engines usually use it as the result headline.

terms.title: Meta description: length, duplicates and snippets
terms.definition: A `<meta name="description">` summary of the page that search engines may use as the result snippet.

terms.title: Heading hierarchy: h1 to h6 for people and parsers
terms.definition: The nesting of h1 to h6 headings that gives a page its outline for readers, screen readers and parsers.

terms.title: Character encoding and mojibake: charset done right
terms.definition: The mapping from bytes to characters (normally UTF-8) declared in the Content-Type header or a meta charset tag; a mismatch produces mojibake.

terms.title: Open Graph tags: what each one controls in a share
terms.definition: A set of og: meta properties (title, description, image, url) that controls how a link previews when it is shared.

terms.title: Internal linking: what counts and what a crawl can see
terms.definition: Links between pages of the same site, which carry crawlers and readers through it and signal which pages matter.

terms.title: What is an orphan page? Finding and fixing them
terms.definition: A page that no other crawled page links to, so crawlers and readers only reach it through a sitemap or a direct URL.

terms.title: Broken links: internal, external and how to find them
terms.definition: A link whose target answers with an error, does not resolve, or is malformed.

terms.title: Anchor text: descriptive links for search and screen readers
terms.definition: The visible, clickable text of a link, which tells readers and search engines what the target is about.
A link attribute value asking search engines not to associate the linking page with the target; a hint, not a block.
A link to an id within a page (#section); it is broken when no element on the target page carries that id.
A link attribute that stops a page opened with `target=_blank` from controlling the page that opened it (tabnabbing).

terms.title: Thin content: what it is and how audits measure it
terms.definition: A page with too little substantive content to be useful, judged here against word count and the site's own norm.
Repeating a term far beyond natural use in the hope of ranking for it, which Google lists as spam.
How hard a text is to read, estimated from sentence and word length with formulas such as Flesch reading ease.

terms.title: Content freshness: dates that agree with each other
terms.definition: How current a page is and how consistently it says so: visible dates, dateModified, sitemap lastmod and copyright year.
Template filler left in production: lorem ipsum text, stock placeholder images, example phone numbers and emails.
Whether the markup parses as intended: closed elements, head-only tags in the head, and no raw markup printed as text.
Text written by a language model; Google's position is that how content is made matters less than whether it is helpful. The related rule is retired and does not run.
terms.grounding_note: ai/ai-content is a cloud rule; say so, and do not claim detection accuracy the rule page does not state.

terms.title: What is structured data? JSON-LD, schema.org and checks
terms.definition: Machine-readable statements about a page's content, usually schema.org vocabulary in JSON-LD, that search engines and agents can parse.

terms.title: What is JSON-LD? Syntax, @id and common errors
terms.definition: JSON for Linking Data, the format Google recommends for structured data, embedded in a `<script type="application/ld+json">` block.

terms.title: Rich results: eligibility, markup and what blocks them
terms.definition: Search result features (stars, breadcrumbs, product prices, video thumbnails) that Google can show when a page has eligible structured data.
FAQPage structured data marking up question-and-answer pairs; Google now shows FAQ rich results only for a narrow set of sites.
terms.grounding_note: Check the rule page for the current Google eligibility statement before writing.

terms.title: Product schema: required fields and rich result checks
terms.definition: Product structured data with offers, price, availability and reviews, used for product rich results and merchant listings.
Article, NewsArticle or BlogPosting structured data with headline, dates, author and publisher.

terms.title: Organization schema: logo, sameAs and one stable @id
terms.definition: Organization structured data naming the business behind a site, its logo, contact points and sameAs profiles.

terms.title: LocalBusiness schema: address, hours and where to put it
terms.definition: LocalBusiness structured data with address, opening hours and geo coordinates for a physical business.
WebSite structured data naming the site, which Google reads for the site name in results, and optionally describing its internal search with a SearchAction.

terms.title: Entities in structured data: one thing, one identity
terms.primary_query: what is an entity in seo
terms.definition: A thing a site describes in structured data, such as an organization, person or product, identified across pages so search engines and agents can tell it is one thing.

terms.title: JSON-LD @id: stable identifiers for your entities
terms.definition: The JSON-LD @id that gives a node a stable IRI, so other nodes and pages can reference the same entity instead of redeclaring it.
VideoObject structured data with name, thumbnail, upload date and duration so a video can appear in video results.

terms.title: Alt text: when to write it, when to leave it empty
terms.definition: The alt attribute that gives an image a text alternative for screen readers, failed loads and search engines.

terms.title: Lazy loading images: below the fold yes, the LCP image no
terms.definition: Deferring off-screen images and iframes with loading="lazy" so they load as the visitor scrolls.

terms.title: Responsive images: srcset, sizes and picture explained
terms.definition: Serving differently sized image files with srcset, sizes and `<picture>` so each device downloads one that fits.
WebP and AVIF, which encode the same image in fewer bytes than JPEG or PNG.
Declared width and height on `` that let the browser reserve space before the file loads, preventing layout shift.

terms.title: What are Core Web Vitals? LCP, INP and CLS defined
terms.definition: Google's three user-experience metrics: LCP for loading, INP for responsiveness and CLS for visual stability, judged at the 75th percentile of real visits.
terms.grounding_note: squirrelscan does not measure the three metrics; its rules flag the page patterns that cause bad values. Say this plainly (matches /learn/core-web-vitals).

terms.title: What is LCP? Largest Contentful Paint and its causes
terms.definition: The time until the largest image or text block in the viewport renders; good is 2.5 seconds or less.

terms.title: What is INP? Interaction to Next Paint explained
terms.definition: The latency from a user interaction to the next frame, taken across the visit; good is 200 milliseconds or less. It replaced FID in March 2024.

terms.title: What is CLS? Cumulative Layout Shift and how to fix it
terms.definition: A score for how much visible content moves unexpectedly while the page is in use; good is 0.1 or less.
The time from the request until the first byte of the response arrives, covering redirects, DNS, connection and server time.

terms.title: Render-blocking resources: what blocks first paint
terms.definition: Stylesheets and synchronous scripts in the head that the browser must fetch before it can paint anything.
An HTML attribute (high, low, auto) that hints how urgently the browser should fetch an image, script or link.
Compressing text responses (HTML, CSS, JS, JSON) with gzip, Brotli or zstd, signalled by Content-Encoding.

terms.title: HTTP caching: Cache-Control for static assets and HTML
terms.definition: Response headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Expires) that let browsers and CDNs reuse a response instead of fetching it again.
Removing whitespace, comments and long names from CSS and JavaScript so the file is smaller without changing behaviour.
The @font-face descriptor (swap, optional, fallback) that decides what text shows while a web font loads.
The number and depth of elements in a page's document tree; large DOMs slow style calculation and interactions.
The total bytes a page downloads across HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images and fonts.
A redirect done in the page (meta refresh or JavaScript) rather than with an HTTP 3xx response.

terms.title: HTTPS for every page: redirects, forms and downgrades
terms.definition: HTTP over TLS, which encrypts traffic and proves the server's identity; every page and form should use it.

terms.title: Security headers: the six every site should send
terms.definition: HTTP response headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) that tell browsers to restrict risky behaviour.

terms.title: What is Content Security Policy? CSP directives explained
terms.definition: A response header listing where a page may load scripts, styles, frames and other resources from, limiting what injected code can do.

terms.title: What is HSTS? max-age, includeSubDomains and preload
terms.definition: The Strict-Transport-Security header that tells browsers to use only HTTPS for a host for a set time.
An HTTPS page loading scripts, styles, images or media over plain HTTP.
An integrity attribute holding a hash of a third-party script or stylesheet, so the browser refuses a tampered file.
A response header that controls whether other sites may embed the page in a frame; CSP frame-ancestors is its successor.
The nosniff header that stops browsers guessing a response's type instead of trusting Content-Type.

terms.title: Cookie attributes: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite and scope
terms.definition: The Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite flags on Set-Cookie that limit where a cookie is sent and whether scripts can read it.
A file at /.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116) that tells researchers how to report a vulnerability.

terms.title: Leaked API keys in the browser: what to look for
terms.definition: Credentials or private keys shipped to the browser in HTML, scripts or source maps.
The GraphQL feature that returns the full schema on request; left on in production it maps the API for attackers.
Where a web app keeps session or auth tokens; tokens in localStorage are readable by any script on the page.

terms.title: How to tell if your website is hacked: the signals
terms.primary_query: how to tell if website is hacked
terms.definition: The traces a compromise leaves on a site: injected pages off the theme, phishing kits, obfuscated scripts and known malicious URLs.
Serving search engines or particular user agents different content from what visitors see, a Google spam policy violation.
A page made to rank for a query and funnel visitors elsewhere, often many near-identical pages per keyword or city.

terms.title: Cookie consent banners: what an audit can verify
terms.definition: The banner and mechanism that asks visitors before setting non-essential cookies, as GDPR and ePrivacy require in the EU.
terms.grounding_note: Not legal advice; say what the rule detects, not what the law requires in detail.

terms.definition: The page explaining what personal data a site collects and why; required by law in many places and a trust signal for search.
Community-maintained rule lists (EasyList, EasyPrivacy) that ad and tracker blockers use to hide elements and block requests.

terms.title: What is WCAG? Levels, criteria and what audits check
terms.definition: The W3C's Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, organised as testable success criteria at levels A, AA and AAA; 2.2 is current.
terms.grounding_note: a11y rules are hand-written, not axe-core; an automated audit covers a subset of WCAG. Say so.

terms.title: What is ARIA? Roles, states and the first rule of ARIA
terms.definition: Accessible Rich Internet Applications: roles, states and properties that describe custom widgets to assistive technology.

terms.title: Accessible names and aria-label: how they are computed
terms.definition: The name assistive technology announces for an element, computed from its content, label, aria-label or aria-labelledby.

terms.title: Color contrast ratio: WCAG AA thresholds and checks
terms.definition: The luminance ratio between text and its background; WCAG AA asks for 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text.
The `<label>` or accessible name tied to each form control, plus autocomplete tokens, so people know what to enter.
The page regions (main, nav, header, footer) that screen reader users jump between, plus the skip link to main content.
Whether every control can be reached and used with a keyboard alone, with a visible focus indicator and sensible tab order.
The lang attribute on `<html>` (and on passages) that declares the language, so screen readers pick the right voice.
Synchronised text of a video's dialogue and sounds, supplied as a `<track kind="captions">` file.
The tappable area of a control; WCAG 2.2 sets 24 by 24 CSS pixels as the AA minimum.

terms.title: Viewport meta tag: width=device-width and zoom
terms.definition: `<meta name="viewport">` that sets the layout width to the device width; disabling zoom in it fails accessibility.

terms.title: Mobile-friendly pages: what a mobile audit checks
terms.definition: A page that works on a phone without zooming or sideways scrolling: viewport set, readable text, tappable controls, no input zoom.

terms.title: URL slugs: length, hyphens, case and special characters
terms.definition: The readable last part of a URL path; short, lowercase, hyphen-separated words work best.
Whether URLs end in /; /page and /page/ are different URLs, so a site should pick one and redirect the other.
Key-value pairs after ? in a URL; tracking and sort parameters can multiply URLs for the same content.

terms.title: What is hreflang? Return links, x-default and errors
terms.definition: Link annotations that tell search engines which language or regional versions of a page exist, with x-default as the fallback.

terms.title: What is E-E-A-T? The signals a site can show
terms.definition: Experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trustworthiness: the qualities Google's quality raters are told to assess, with trust at the centre.
terms.grounding_note: E-E-A-T is not a ranking factor or score; rules detect on-page signals only.

terms.title: What is YMYL? Your Money or Your Life content explained
terms.definition: Topics that could significantly affect a person's health, finances, safety or society, which Google's raters hold to a higher standard.
The visible author name on an article, ideally linked to an author page and matched by an author entity in structured data.
A clear statement that a page earns commission from links, required by the FTC in the US and similar rules elsewhere.

terms.title: What is NAP in local SEO? Consistency and checks
terms.definition: Name, address and phone number stated the same way across a site's pages, schema and listings.

terms.title: Geo meta tags: geo.position, placename and their limits
terms.definition: Legacy geo.region, geo.placename and geo.position meta tags that state a page's location; not to be confused with GEO, generative engine optimization.
terms.grounding_note: GSC shows 'geo placename' and 'geo meta tags' queries on /rules/local/geo-meta: this term disambiguates from GEO.

terms.definition: Finding the topics and queries a site's audience searches for that the site does not yet cover. The related rules are opt-in and run only when selected explicitly.
terms.grounding_note: Cloud, opt-in, uses live search data.

terms.title: What is agent experience (AX)? Five pillars, checked
terms.definition: How well a site serves AI agents that read it, find their way around it and act on it, the way UX serves people.
terms.grounding_note: Canonical term. Never 'agent readiness' or 'AI readiness' (Cloudflare's product name may be cited as a proper noun only).

terms.title: What is GEO? Generative engine optimization defined
terms.definition: Making content more likely to be retrieved, cited and quoted by AI answer engines; the term comes from a 2023 research paper.
terms.grounding_note: No rule measures GEO directly. List the rules that bear on whether an AI system can reach and parse the page; no ranking claims. /learn owns the long guide; this page is the definition.

terms.title: What is llms.txt? Format, adoption and what it is not
terms.definition: A proposed Markdown file at /llms.txt that gives language models a curated map of a site's key content.
terms.grounding_note: Google has said it does not use llms.txt for ranking; keep that line from the AX hub.

terms.definition: A Markdown file of instructions for coding agents working in a repository or against a docs site.

terms.title: AI crawlers: GPTBot, ClaudeBot and what to allow
terms.definition: A bot that fetches pages for AI companies, in three classes: training crawlers, AI search indexers and user-triggered fetchers, each with its own user-agent token.
Content-Signal lines in robots.txt that state whether content may be used for search, AI input or AI training.
Meta robots values some sites use to ask AI systems not to train on their text or images; not part of any standard search engines honour.
A standard for publishing machine-readable licensing terms for AI use of content, referenced from robots.txt.
Charging AI crawlers for access with HTTP 402 Payment Required responses, as in Cloudflare Pay Per Crawl and the x402 protocol.
Serving a clean Markdown version of a page, through Accept: text/markdown or a .md URL, so agents read fewer tokens.

terms.title: Client-side rendering: what agents and crawlers miss
terms.definition: Building page content in the browser with JavaScript; agents and many fetchers that do not run JavaScript see an empty page.
Fixed paths under /.well-known/ (RFC 8615) where sites publish machine-readable files: security.txt, api-catalog, OAuth metadata and agent manifests.
